title: Job hunting: pitch a small company with a specific fix instead of mass-applying
summary: Priyam Raj argues students should skip the traditional DSA-and-apply path and instead target small niche companies. Study the product, find something concrete to fix or improve, and pitch the founder directly with genuine enthusiasm and a low ask. He says this landed one of his first jobs at over 2 lakhs a month.

principles.text: Target small, niche companies instead of mass-applying through the traditional path.
principles.quote: why don't you follow this route route of, you know, just targeting a very niche small specific company?

principles.text: Reach out organically to the founder or product manager, not with a templated AI-style email.
principles.quote: Reach out to the founder founders, product manager, whoever you think would be the best option in that specific case. And offer them your help.

principles.text: Study the product first, then pitch a specific feature to add, bug to fix or thing to improve.
principles.quote: talk about, you know, that specific feature you can add or specific thing you can fix or improve.

principles.text: Pitch how you will help the company, not that you need a job.
principles.quote: you have to pitch in a way where it sounds like you're going to help the person.

principles.text: Founders prefer hiring people enthusiastic about the product over people who just need help.
principles.quote: as a founder, I would any day want to hire someone who you know, who has more enthusiasm about my product rather than someone needing help.

principles.text: A specific, product-aware pitch with a low-cost ask vastly outperforms a generic plea.
principles.quote: This kind of a pitch would 100% would be like, I don't know seven times better than, you know, something that's like very general.
